faq.nota: Sample answers for this demo mockup.

preguntas.a: Standard delivery is FREE on orders over $35; otherwise it’s $5.99. Express delivery is $12.99. You’ll see the delivery date before you pay.

preguntas.q: Why isn’t sales tax included in the price?
preguntas.a: In the US, prices are shown before tax because the rate depends on where you live. The cart estimates the tax with your ZIP code, and checkout calculates the exact amount.

preguntas.q: Can I see a toy in a store before buying?
preguntas.a: Yes. On each toy, “Check store availability” shows which store near you has it in stock. The stores in this demo are samples.
Yes, within 30 days if it’s unused and in its original box. This is a sample policy.

preguntas.q: Which payment methods do you accept?
preguntas.a: Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal and pay in 4 installments. In this demo nothing is charged.
No. You can check out as a guest with just an email. An account lets you see your orders, buy again and keep a wish list.

preguntas.q: How do I know a toy is right for my child’s age?
preguntas.a: Each toy shows its age range and any safety warnings, such as small parts for children under 3.

preguntas.q: What do you do with my data?
preguntas.a: This demo doesn’t collect personal data: your cart and account are saved only in your browser. The real store will have a full privacy policy, including “Your Privacy Choices”.

panel.subtitulo: Last 30 days compared with the 30 days before.
panel.fraseTicket: Each order is worth {monto} on average.
panel.explicaVentas: All the money customers paid for toys in these 30 days, before tax and shipping.
panel.explicaPedidos: How many purchases were made. One order can have several toys.
panel.explicaTicket: Sales divided by orders: how much a customer spends each time they buy. Bundles and free shipping over $35 help raise it.
panel.explicaGrafico: Each point is one day. When the solid line is above the dashed one, you’re selling more than before. Weekends sell more.
panel.caminoFrase: Out of every 100 visitors, {carrito} add a toy to the cart and {compran} buy.
panel.explicaCamino: It shows where people leave. The biggest drop is the first thing worth improving.
panel.explicaMasVendidos: Your top 5 toys by units sold in the last 30 days. Make sure they never run out.
panel.explicaStock: How many units each place has. “Online” is the warehouse that ships web orders; the stores only show what customers can find in person.
panel.explicaVisitas: How many times someone came into the store. If the same person comes back another day, it counts again.
panel.fraseClics: {n} out of every 100 visits open a toy’s page.
panel.explicaClics: How many times a toy’s page was opened. It’s the sign that something caught their eye.
panel.fraseConversion: Out of every 100 visits, {n} end in a purchase.
panel.explicaConversion: Orders divided by visits. For toy stores it’s usually between 1% and 3%: raising it a little is worth more than getting more visits.
panel.explicaAbandonados: People who added something to the cart and didn’t buy. In the real store they can get a reminder email.

enVivo.titulo: Live: what’s happening in this demo
enVivo.texto: What you do in the store from this browser shows up here right away. Nothing is sent anywhere.
enVivo.vacio: No activity yet. Open the store, look at toys, add one to the cart and buy it: you’ll see it here.

panel.explicaHoras: Orders from the last 30 days by time of day. It’s a good time to post on social media or send emails.
panel.explicaEstados: The states with the most orders. It helps decide where to advertise or open another store.
panel.fraseEstrella: {n} sold and {monto} in 30 days. Out of every 100 people who look at it, {conv} buy it.
panel.explicaClicsVentas: How many times each page was opened, added to the cart and sold. If a toy gets lots of looks and few sales, check its price, photos or description.
panel.interesSinVentas: Lots of interest, few sales: “{producto}” has {clics} clicks and only {conv} buy it. Check its price or photos.
panel.explicaBusquedas: What people type in the search box. Searches with no results are toys they want and you don’t have.
panel.teFaltan: They ask for these and you don’t have them: {lista}.
panel.explicaOrigen: Where people came in from and how many orders came from each. If a channel brings visits and few purchases, check what you post there.
panel.explicaDispositivos: Which device they visit and buy from. If phones buy less, the phone checkout is the first thing to review.
panel.fraseClientes: {pct} of orders come from customers who had bought before.
panel.explicaClientes: Bringing a customer back costs less than finding a new one. Wish lists and reminder emails help.
